Perfect! After **Be5+**, White's rook is hanging on d6. All king moves allow Black to capture it with **Bxd6**, winning the rook (worth 5 points vs the 3-point bishop). The cleanest line is **Be5+ Kf3 Bxd6**. This is a textbook fork motif.

**Coaching Note:**

Your opponent's king and rook were on the same diagonal after moving to f4. When your bishop can give check from e5, it forks both pieces—the king must move and loses the rook. Always scan for pieces aligned on diagonals or lines; a timely check can trap a defender. This rook fork won the game.
